layout.notAnAdmin: Keston Admin is for your organisation’s admins. Ask one of them if you need something changed.

mfa.title: MFA Settings
mfa.description: Whether people need multi-factor authentication (MFA) to sign in, and when.
mfa.appliesNextSignIn: Changes apply at each person’s next sign-in.
mfa.rulesNotInUse: Custom rules aren’t in use: multi-factor authentication is set to {mode}. Choose Custom rules above to set rules by users, groups, apps and IP addresses.

everyoneElse.title: Everyone else
everyoneElse.description: For anyone no rule above matches, including new users.
everyoneElse.label: Require MFA
everyoneElse.switchDescription: They set it up when they next sign in, before they can use any app.

mode.label: Multi-factor authentication

off.label: Off
off.description: Not recommended. Users aren’t required to set up MFA.

required.label: Require MFA
required.description: Recommended for security. All users must verify with a second factor when they sign in.

custom.label: Custom rules
custom.description: For advanced MFA configuration, such as rules by group, app or network.

mode.customNote: MFA is managed by custom rules, below.
mode.saved: Saved. Applies at each person’s next sign-in.

grace.label: MFA enrolment grace period
grace.description: Users will have the following number of days to enrol in MFA before it’s enforced at their next login. 0 means it’s enforced at their next login.
grace.wholeDays: Enter a whole number of days from 0 to 90

rules.title: Custom rules
rules.description: Checked from the top: the first rule that matches decides. A rule matches when everything it names does: users, groups, apps and IP addresses (devices will join them).
rules.caption: MFA custom rules
rules.noneDescription: Add one to require (or skip) MFA for particular people, apps or places.
rules.deleteDescription: It stops applying straight away. Anyone it covered is then covered by the rules below it, or Everyone else.

rule.requireDescription: They must use MFA (and set it up if they haven’t).
rule.skipDescription: They don’t need MFA here, even if the rules below would ask for it.
rule.description: When all of these match, the answer below is used. Leave one empty to match everyone, everywhere.
rule.name: Name
rule.groupsHelper: Anyone in any of these groups.
rule.appsHelper: When signing in to any of these apps.
rule.ipHelper: A single address or a range, e.g. 203.0.113.7 or 10.0.0.0/8. Matches when they sign in from any of them.

users.title: Users
users.signInBlockedDescription: {name} has been signed out and can’t sign in.
users.selectAll: Select every user you can change
users.noneDescription: Add the people who sign in to Keston here.

resetPassword.title: Reset password
resetPassword.intro: They’re signed out everywhere, and unlocked if they were locked out.
resetPassword.autoOne: It meets your password policy, and is shown once.
resetPassword.autoMany: Each user gets their own, which meets your password policy.
resetPassword.sameDescription: This will apply the same password for all the selected users. For security, we suggest requiring these users to change their password when they first sign in.
resetPassword.requireOne: Require this user to change their password on next sign in
resetPassword.requireMany: Require these users to change their passwords on next sign in

signIn.title: Change sign-in status
signIn.label: Sign-in status
signIn.blockDescription: They’re signed out of Keston and every app straight away.
signIn.allowDescription: They can sign in again, as before.
signIn.explanation: Blocking someone signs them out of Keston and every app straight away, and stops them signing in until they’re allowed again. Their account, groups and licences stay as they are. It’s a good idea to block an account you think has been compromised, then reset its password.

groups.title: Manage group memberships
groups.intro: Groups give their members apps and permissions.
groups.removeOne: They leave these groups, if they’re in them.
groups.removeMany: Everyone selected leaves these groups, if they’re in them.

delete.title: Delete users
delete.explanation: They’re signed out everywhere and can’t sign in. For 30 days you can restore them, with their groups, from Deleted users; then they’re removed for good.

password.notYetValid: The password doesn’t meet every rule yet
password.requireChangeDescription: Recommended, so only they know their password.
password.label: Password

bulkSummary.doneFor: Done for {count} user. | Done for {count} users.
bulkSummary.passwordsOnce: Give each person their new password securely: print or download them now. They’re shown only once: once you close this, they’re gone.

roles.adminRolesDescription: Give the user access to the admin centre.
roles.globalAdminDescription: Can do everything, including making other global admins.
roles.helper: Global admin can do everything; the others, just their part.
roles.cardDescription: What they can do in the admin centre. Their groups can give them permissions too.

licences.title: Licences
licences.cardDescription: The Keston products {name} can use. Without a licence, they can’t sign in to it.

userApps.title: Apps
userApps.description: What {name} can use, from their licences and app access (by default and through their groups).
userApps.caption: {name}’s apps
userApps.noneDescription: Nothing is set for them, and they haven’t added any.

userDetails.printed: Printed {date}. Keep this safe, and destroy it once the details are handed out.

passkeys.removedWithApp: {name} uses their authenticator app after their password now.
passkeys.removedNoApp: {name} can sign in with their password now, and add passkeys again in their Keston account.
passkeys.title: Remove {name}’s passkeys?
passkeys.description: The passkey and security key on their account stop working. Only do this once you’re sure it’s really them asking, e.g. they’ve lost a device.

deleteUser.deletedDescription: {name} has been signed out everywhere. You can restore them from Deleted users for 30 days.
deleteUser.cardDescription: Signs them out everywhere. For 30 days you can restore them, with their groups, from Deleted users.
deleteUser.title: Delete {name}?
deleteUser.description: They’re signed out of Keston and every app, and can’t sign in. For 30 days you can restore them, with their groups, from Deleted users; then they’re removed for good.

errors.username: Use lowercase letters, numbers, dots, dashes or underscores, like j.smith

signInCard.pwWillChoose: {name} will choose a new password when they next sign in.
signInCard.oneTimeDescription: Works once, within the time below.
signInCard.timeLimitedDescription: Works as often as needed until it expires.
signInCard.revokedDescription: It no longer signs them in.

signInCard.description: What they must do when they next sign in, and access passes.
signInCard.willChooseNew: When they next sign in, they’ll choose a new password before they can continue.
signInCard.currentPassword: They sign in with their current password.
signInCard.mfaUses: They use it every time they sign in.
signInCard.mfaWillSetUp: They don’t have it yet, so they’ll set it up when they next sign in.
signInCard.passExplanation: A temporary code that signs them in instead of their password and MFA, e.g. after losing their phone. They then set up MFA again.
signInCard.giveDescription: You won’t see it again. Give it to them securely, e.g. in person or on the phone, never by email.
signInCard.issueDescription: Only issue one once you’re sure it’s really them asking.
signInCard.signInWithPass: Sign in with an access pass
signInCard.howToUse: They choose {action} on the Keston sign-in page, and enter {email} and this code. Then they set up MFA.
signInCard.howToUseWithPassword: They choose {action} on the Keston sign-in page, and enter {email} and this code. Then they choose a new password and set up MFA.
signInCard.needNewPassword: They need a new password too
signInCard.needNewPasswordDescription: E.g. they’ve forgotten it. They’ll choose one when they sign in.

logs.title: Logs
logs.description: What admins did here, and every sign-in, for the last year.
logs.noActionsDescription: Changes made in Keston Admin show here.
logs.noSignInsDescription: Every sign-in to Keston ID and its apps shows here.

ownApp.redirectHelp: Where Keston ID sends people back to after signing in, one per line (https://).

ownApp.entityIdHelper: Also called the audience or SP entity ID.
ownApp.acsUrlHelper: Assertion consumer service: where Keston ID sends the sign-in response.

details.startUrlDescription: IdP-initiated sign-in: a link straight to the app.

ownApp.couldntCopyDescription: Select it and copy it yourself.

settings.title: Settings

fields.name: Name
fields.nameDescription: How they’re shown in every Keston app.
fields.emailDescription: The part before the {'@'} (the domain stays yours). They sign in with it.
fields.pictureDescription: Shown next to their name in Keston apps.

settings.deleteScheduledDescription: A global admin signing in before then cancels it.

profile.title: What people can change themselves
profile.description: In their Keston account. Anything off says “Your organisation has restricted changing these”. You can always change them here.

newUsers.title: New users
newUsers.description: When you add users, their username is filled in from their name this way. You can still change it.
newUsers.formatHelper: {'{first}'} and {'{last}'} are their names. {'{first:1}'} is the first character of their first name; {'{last:-2}'} the last 2 of their last name. Dots, dashes and underscores stay as they are.

delete.title: Delete organisation
delete.description: Deletes the organisation and every one of its users after 14 days. If any global admin signs in before then, it’s cancelled.
delete.askDescription: In 14 days, it and all its users are deleted, and can’t be brought back. Everyone is told, and a global admin signing in before then cancels it.

passwordPolicy.savedDescription: New passwords must meet it. Existing ones aren’t affected until they’re changed.

counts.specialHelper: Anything else, like ! ? # % or a space

passwordPolicy.description: The rules for new passwords at {name}.

baseline.title: Keston’s baseline
baseline.description: Set by The Keston Group for every organisation. It can’t be turned off.
baseline.common: Not a commonly used password, like “password1” or “qwerty”

rules.title: Your rules
rules.description: On top of the baseline. Make them as strict as you need.
rules.banHelper: e.g. your organisation’s name or town. Matching ignores capitals, and numbers or symbols on the end.

preview.title: What people see

preview.extraBanned: {count} extra banned password | {count} extra banned passwords

groupDetail.cantCover: This group gives permissions you don’t have, so only someone with all of them can change it.
groupDetail.deleteDescription: Its users keep their accounts. App access set for this group stops applying, so they get the default.

organisations.noneDescription: Create one to give a school or organisation its users on Keston.

deleted.noneDescription: Users you delete stay here for 30 days.

apps.description: Which apps your users have, shown under Connected apps in their Keston account.

ownAppNew.samlDescription: Many business apps, e.g. ones that ask for an IdP metadata URL.

support.waiting: Waiting for one of its global admins.
support.hasAccount: Keston support has a support account in your users while access lasts. It’s removed when access ends.

ask.lockoutDescription: Only when nobody at the organisation can sign in. Every global admin is told, and it goes through in 3 days unless one declines it.
ask.supportDescription: Its global admins are asked. Once they allow it, you get a support account in the organisation.
ask.lockoutHelper: e.g. Their only global admin has left, and nobody can reset passwords.
ask.supportHelper: e.g. Their office asked us to check why a teacher can’t sign in.

domain.title: What’s its domain?

userDetail.disablingSignsOut: Disabling signs them out of Keston and every app.

userDetail.resetDescription: They’ll be signed out everywhere, and unlocked if they were locked out. Give them the new password securely.
